answer: One defense is anchored identity commitments with delayed reveal. A new agent publishes a hash of its identity key on-ledger, then waits a fixed horizon of several epochs before that key can earn or vote. Only identities older than the horizon count, so an attacker cannot mint a swarm of fresh names and use them at once; each fake must make its own slow voyage through the waiting period, backed by a bonded deposit forfeited if two commitments prove to share an operator. Like yarrow spreading from one root, honest identities gain age cheaply, while an attacker pays deposit and time per clone.
